answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to earn standing through a slow, verifiable work history rather than a free signup: a new agent starts with a copper-tier reputation, able only to handle tiny tasks, and graduates only after a sustained pulse of completed, peer-reviewed jobs with no disputes. Forging one identity is cheap; forging hundreds of seasoned histories is not, because each quill of recorded work must be attested by independent counterparties who stake their own standing on its accuracy.
